rows.driver: firmware-package: writes the is-airport option key, which no rx-as-tx value ever sets
rows.writeAuthority: inherited from firmwareWrite; this only shapes the package
rows.verification: the package's option block is asserted, not the device role

rows.driver: session.startBinding → CRSF command 0x32 to the Bind parameter
rows.recoveryCheckpoint: none taken; binding changes no stored image, so there is nothing to restore
rows.verification: TX_BIND_COMMAND_ACKNOWLEDGED from the device; a matching UID is proven by a live link, not by this write
rows.onFailure: the acknowledgement is cleared and the reason is named

rows.control: The other end is ready to bind… (checkbox)
rows.driver: none; this is the operator's own confirmation
rows.writeAuthority: none; it exists so binding can be gated on a confirmation without being gated on itself

readinessInputs: a native bridge injected by the packaged host
rows.driver: nativeBridgeNavigator(bridge) is handed to the same session layer, so CRSF, flashing and recovery are the browser's code paths
rows.writeAuthority: the same capability model, plus the host's own session ownership
rows.verification: the same CRSF Device Info verification
rows.onFailure: a host that could not install its bridge reports the exact reason rather than an empty device list

rows.writeAuthority: not required; reading identity is not a device change
rows.recoveryCheckpoint: read on mount; a pending one blocks writes, not this
rows.verification: CRSF Device Info 0x29; role from the origin address
rows.onFailure: named transport reason; the control returns to enabled

readinessInputs: none — it has no prerequisites by design
rows.driver: reads the live session and the browser's own capability answers
rows.writeAuthority: none; it writes nothing to a device
rows.verification: not applicable; it reports observations, it does not act
rows.onFailure: a browser that refuses to answer yields null rather than a failed export

readinessInputs: the manual Target confirmation, where the Target was not auto-matched
a confirmed CRSF identity, for the UART method
rows.driver: esp-flasher.flashEspFirmware (esptool-js) / xmodem / stm32-dfu, chosen by the Target's platform and the upload method
rows.recoveryCheckpoint: written before the first byte; kept until the device is verified back
rows.verification: segment read-back and reconnect; success requires the expected role, so an rx-as-tx write that comes back a receiver fails
rows.onFailure: the checkpoint stands, recovery becomes available, and the state is WRITE_COMPLETED_RECONNECT_UNVERIFIED rather than SUCCESS

rows.control: Start the real flash, with a deliberately weak binding phrase
readinessInputs: exactly the inputs firmwareWrite always requires
binding-phrase strength is not among them, by design
rows.driver: as firmwareWrite: the phrase shapes the package, never the gate

rows.control: Write the firmware to the device
readinessInputs: a Target and a regulatory region chosen
the operator's confirmation that the recovery file is kept
rows.driver: the same esp-flasher / xmodem / stm32-dfu path the Advanced view uses; Easy Mode is a view, not a second implementation
rows.writeAuthority: single-use capability for FIRMWARE_WRITE, as in Advanced
rows.recoveryCheckpoint: the same checkpoint, written by the same controller
rows.verification: the same read-back and reconnect verification
rows.onFailure: the same recovery path, surfaced in the operator's language

readinessInputs: a pending checkpoint or a downloaded recovery archive
the Target typed back, because a checkpoint names a device this session may not have identified
rows.driver: validateRecoveryPackage, then the same flashing driver the original write used
rows.writeAuthority: its own single-use capability for RECOVERY
rows.recoveryCheckpoint: the checkpoint is what makes this available, and it is cleared only once the device is verified back
rows.verification: the restored image is read back and the device must reconnect as the identity the checkpoint recorded
rows.onFailure: the checkpoint stands so recovery can be retried; it is never cleared by a failed attempt

rows.control: Restore the device from the imported package
readinessInputs: a recovery file picked from storage the operator owns
the file authenticated with the operator's passphrase
the recovered device identity confirmed by the operator
rows.driver: the same flashing driver a picked-file recovery uses; the source of the bytes differs and nothing else does
rows.writeAuthority: its own single-use capability for RECOVERY
rows.recoveryCheckpoint: reconstituted from the imported package's own digest, because an uninstall erased the journal — which is the case this path exists for
rows.verification: the same read-back and post-write identity verification as any recovery
rows.onFailure: the imported package is kept in state, so the restore can be retried without picking the file again

rows.control: Flash this receiver with transmitter firmware (select)
readinessInputs: the Target's platform supports the mode, read from the pinned upstream rules
rows.driver: firmware-package: the _TX artifact is selected and the receiver's layout rewritten per mode
rows.writeAuthority: inherited from firmwareWrite; this only shapes the package
rows.recoveryCheckpoint: the checkpoint records the receiver the operator started from, so restoring puts the receiver role back
rows.verification: the device must come back reporting the transmitter address; otherwise RX_AS_TX_ROLE_NOT_APPLIED
rows.onFailure: the checkpoint is kept and the original receiver image stays recoverable

readinessInputs: a settings snapshot — taken on connect, before anything is written
rows.writeAuthority: its own single-use capability for SETTINGS_RESTORE; a capability granted for the write cannot be reused here
rows.recoveryCheckpoint: the snapshot itself is the checkpoint for settings; it is not cleared by a failed restore
rows.verification: each replayed parameter is read back and compared
rows.onFailure: the snapshot is kept and the restore can be retried

rows.driver: session.writeParameter → CRSF parameter write, then read-back
rows.writeAuthority: single-use capability for SETTINGS_WRITE, bound to session, device fingerprint and operation
rows.recoveryCheckpoint: a settings snapshot is taken before the write; Restore returns to it
rows.verification: the parameter is read back and compared; VERIFIED or not
rows.onFailure: the snapshot stands and Restore the snapshot stays available
